title: [Service Container] Inlining property-injected service definitions generates invalid XML
body:
Hello,

Defining a private service then injecting it only once will cause its definition to be dumped 'inline' when generating a cached service definitions XML file (which is expected in the dev environment). However, when this service is injected using property injection, the following error occurs:

```
 [InvalidArgumentException]

 [ERROR 1871] Element '{http://symfony.com/schema/dic/services}service':
 This element is not expected. (in [...] /app/cache/dev/appDevDebugProjectContainer.xml [...] )
```

The cached services definitions XML files contains the following chunk, which is indeed invalid:

```
  <property name="[...]" type="service">
    <service class="[...]" public="false">
      [...]
    </service>
  </property>
```

You can reproduce the issue by adding the following snippet in a services definitions XML file:

```
<services>
    <service id="foo" class="StdClass" public="false" />
    <service id="bar" class="StdClass">
        <property name="p" type="service" id="foo" />
    </service>
</services>
```

Temporary workaround: Make that service definition public so it does not get inlined.

When it comes to a permanent fix, I am not sure about whether the xsd should accept inlined definitions of property-injected services (see: https://groups.google.com/group/symfony-devs/browse_thread/thread/d4ad8626db8316c3 for a somewhat related issue) or if property-injected services should just skip inlining.

All the best,
## 

mirsal
